text: After this you can connect each functional requirement to a suitable test result.

A functional configuration audit looks at whether the accepted behavior of a defined configuration has been demonstrated. Start with its requirements, then follow each one to a test method, measured result and disposition. Confirm the identity of the item used for the test. An earlier test report may help. It cannot automatically prove that a later, changed version meets the same requirement.

items: Identify accepted functions and performance limits. You should see: Each requirement has a clear pass condition. If not: Clarify vague words such as "adequate."
Locate the corresponding procedures and results. You should see: The result addresses the intended requirement. If not: Record any untested or inconclusive function.
Confirm the tested item configuration. You should see: The evidence applies to the version under audit. If not: Assess whether differences affect validity.
List gaps and decisions for follow-up. You should see: Open issues have owners and proof needed. If not: Do not mark a requirement satisfied by assertion.
Inferred: A timed operation needs a specified limit and accepted test. Record the result and tested software version.

text: Link every functional claim to evidence from the relevant version.
A successful demonstration may not cover abnormal or failure conditions.

items: Using a test result without a test-item identity No one can tell whether it applies to the current version. Fix: Record the tested revision or evaluate its relevance.
